title: Spawn & Sunset Pier
where: The first stretch below the hamlet road, including the mainland around Sunset Pier.
problem: Ground meets the sea without a continuous authored beach; the small cove sand pad does not cover this frontage.
proposal: A 20–35 m pale sand crescent below the road, with two short dark rock shoulders and a gently submerged sand shelf. Keep the pier, road and island crossing clear.
access: Low coastal steps beside the existing detour lane; an uninterrupted walkable dry strip where slope allows.

title: Hidamari south & harbor
tagline: A working waterfront, with breathing room
where: The full southern city frontage, harbor entrance and canal mouth.
problem: The city has its own water sheet 2.5 cm above the main sea. The broad lawn-to-water boundary lacks a continuous beach or quay treatment.
proposal: Keep the working quay and breakwater. Add 15–25 m sand pockets to either side, with stone revetments only under built waterfronts. Keep the canal opening and boat approach open.
access: Quay stairs reach the sand pockets; no rocks across navigable water.

title: Far east / city headland
where: The southeast corner and east-facing terrain beyond the city, continuing north to y=900.
problem: The detailed city ends well before the coarse backdrop edge. The outer terrain is a rectangular open edge, rather than a designed coastal profile.
proposal: A scalloped rocky headland with 15–45 m faces and 10–20 m sandy coves at the low points. Regrade the outer backdrop inside its current envelope; extend the rock toe below water.
access: One coastal lookout and a safe descent near the city; remote cliff toes remain boat-only.

title: Volcano east / railway coast
where: Eastern outer coast beside the volcano and inland railway corridor.
problem: The far-hill mesh stops at x=3200 with elevated open edges; the railway rounds the volcano inland at x≈2450.
proposal: Stepped charcoal rock headlands, 30–80 m cliff faces and occasional gravel coves. Preserve the railway corridor and its earthworks. Use broad rock masses that read from the summit.
access: Keep cliff rims outside the railway clearance; descents only at naturally low coves.

title: Belmonte east coast
where: Eastern country outside Belmonte, north of the volcano corridor.
problem: The north-country inland mask becomes exactly zero at x≥3000. That creates a broad coplanar terrain apron under the sea.
proposal: Two or three generous 30–60 m ochre sand bays separated by low rocky points. Replace the zero-height apron with a sloping submerged shelf; keep Belmonte’s valley and railway untouched.
access: Country paths descend from inland; beach scale should remain legible from the volcano.

title: Northern cape
tagline: A proper end to the island
where: The complete northern closure, including the northwest and northeast turns.
problem: The country is multiplied by smooth((7100−y)/1000): it reaches z=0 exactly at the last row. The north edge has no submerged continuation.
proposal: A broad shallow crescent interrupted by two rocky capes and a few low dunes. Establish a finite dry shore before the terrain boundary, then sink the final rows safely below the sea.
access: A quiet distant destination; no extra landmark or settlement needed.

title: Belmonte west coast
where: Western north-country coast outside the imported Belmonte valley.
problem: The same inland mask reaches zero at x≤−3000. The exported grid carries that flat strip along most of the western country.
proposal: An alternating rhythm of 25–50 m sand coves and 10–30 m wooded rock bluffs, with a deeper sheltered bay in the middle. Remove the coplanar shelf all along this side.
access: A small number of connecting country paths; keep the inland authored valley intact.

title: Western volcano coast
where: The long western outer terrain edge opposite the volcanic highlands.
problem: The coarse far-hill grid is clipped at x=−3200 while still elevated; its open mesh edge offers no sea cliff face or submerged toe.
proposal: A sequence of 40–100 m rugged cliffs with long rock shelves and sparse pebble landings. Carve broad inlets inside the current boundary and close the terrain below the sea.
access: Boat access to a few shelves; no continuous path forced onto steep cliffs.

title: Southwest outer coast
tagline: A wild coast that softens toward home
where: Southwestern mainland from the western edge back toward the hamlet and spawn bay.
problem: The backdrop’s southern sea crossing exists, but uses coarse grass-covered cells; the western corner is still a clipped high terrain edge.
proposal: Scalloped 10–40 m wooded headlands with a few pale sand and pebble pockets. Gradually lower the cliffs toward the spawn crescent so the coast has one continuous silhouette.
access: Retain open sailing water toward the temple islet; remote pockets can remain boat-only.

title: Temple islet & landing
tagline: Keep the rocks. Make the landing belong.
where: The entire separate southwest temple islet, including the north-facing landing and sea stacks.
problem: This already has authored 8–38 m cliffs and a small sand cove. It needs a waterline and landing continuity pass, rather than wholesale replacement.
proposal: Retain the current cliff silhouette and four stacks. Broaden only the landing cove into a 12–20 m usable beach, tie its sand into the stair approach and carry wet rock below water.
access: Keep the existing landing, stair, gates and temple; preserve the boat crossing.
